p: In the prayer of Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,
corresponds to Yaakov our forefather, peace be upon him.
would belong more in the blessing "Atah Gibbor,"
שֶׁהוּא כְּנֶגֶד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
which corresponds to Yitzchak our forefather, peace be upon him,
whose attribute is "the Fear of Yitzchak."
The matter is, as is known,
"the Great, the Mighty, and the Awesome"
correspond to the holiness of the three Avos:
correspond to the attributes of Gedulah and Gevurah,
for Avraham our forefather, peace be upon him,
and Yitzchak our forefather, peace be upon him,
our forefather, peace be upon him,
"The G-d before Whom my fathers walked"
that they served through their own effort,
Avraham with the attribute of love
and Yitzchak with the attribute of fear.
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ כְּלוּם,
for he has nothing through his own effort,
only what Hashem, may He be blessed,
illuminates for him and shepherds him.
And he said, "From where will my help come?
לֵית אֲנָא מוֹבֵיד סִבְרִי מִן בָּרְיִי,
"I will not abandon my hope in my Creator,"
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סח, ב; רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת וַיֵּצֵא)
and also the lowly ones, like the earth
Therefore his attribute corresponds to the description "the Awesome,"
meaning that there falls upon him
fear and dread of Hashem, may He be blessed,
For the attribute of Yitzchak our forefather, peace be upon him,
that Hashem, may He be blessed, stands before him,
and when he sees that the King of the kings of kings,
the Holy One, blessed be He, stands over him,
אֲבָל מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
But the attribute of Yaakov our forefather, peace be upon him,
And it is found in the Gemara (Pesachim 88a):
"Not like Avraham, of whom it wrote 'mountain', etc.,
and not like Yitzchak, of whom it wrote 'field', etc.,
but like Yaakov, who called it 'house.'"
Meaning: whenever the dread comes from man's side,
that the King of the kings of kings stands over him,
זֶה אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ קִיּוּם עוֹד,
שֶׁיִּצְרוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו בְּכָל יוֹם
for a person's inclination overpowers him every day
and renews itself against him every day
where fear falls from Hashem's side,
And this is why it says "who called it 'house'":
when he said "How awesome is this place,"
סִיֵּים ״אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם בֵּית אֱלֹהִים״ —
he concluded, "This is none other than the house of G-d" —
And this is what they said in the Pesikta for Rosh Hashanah
"'Sound the teruah to the G-d of Yaakov' (Tehillim 81:2) —
why Yaakov of all the Avos?
'In the measure with which a person measures,' etc.
It is like a king who had
'By your life, I will build it
and call it the House of Yaakov,' etc.
mentioned only Yaakov with the teruah,
as it says, 'Sound the teruah to the G-d of Yaakov.'"
Seemingly, how is this a reason
to its being called "the House of the G-d of Yaakov"
and "the captivity of the tents of Yaakov."
But the matter is according to what was said,
that the mitzvah of teruah is
to arouse fear in the heart,
"Shall a shofar be blown in a city
And the main thing is that the fear should remain
and this is the attribute of Yaakov, "the Awesome,"
where the dread falls from Hashem of itself,
and this remains in the heart permanently,
and this is why he called it "house."
And so it is written in the Tikkunim
"'And the teruah of the King is in him' —
here you have that teruah is in Yaakov."
And this is the intent of the Pesikta,
which mentioned only "Sound the teruah to the G-d of Yaakov"
And that is because he knew
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתוֹ כְּלָל,
that he has nothing at all through his own effort,
only what Hashem, may He be blessed, radiates —
the fear and dread from His side.
which is the blessing of Yaakov,
the prayer "And so, place Your awe,
Meaning, that Hashem, may He be blessed,
should place the dread from His side,
which is the attribute of Yaakov,
and the fear will remain forever.
even though free choice is given into man's hand,
nevertheless the dominion is before You.
וְאִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁעוֹזֵר לוֹ
"Were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He, helps him,
'Hashem will not abandon him into his hand.'"
And we say, "Strength is in Your hand
and might in Your right hand,"
which is the inclusion of the attribute of Chesed in Gevurah
"Hashem will give strength to His people"
"From His right hand, a fiery law for them,"
and His right hand is the aspect of Chesed.
"In Your hand" alludes to the left hand
when it is mentioned alongside the right
and this is "strength in Your hand" —
the inclusion of Chesed in Gevurah;
this is the inclusion of Gevurah in Chesed.
And from the inclusion of the two attributes
comes the attribute of Yaakov, the aspect of "awesome";
and this is "and Your Name is awesome
over all that You have created."
And the conclusion of the blessing,
"You are holy and Your Name is awesome":
"holy," which is the attribute of Yaakov
our forefather, peace be upon him,
"And they will sanctify the Holy One of Yaakov,"
and this is "and Your Name is awesome," etc.
"And Hashem of Hosts is exalted through judgment":
we have already said that the term "great,"
when said of Hashem, may He be blessed,
and it is the aspect of "Atika."
And Yaakov is "the middle bar," etc.
which holds on to Atika Kaddisha
"He made Avraham in the secret of Chochmah,
Yitzchak in the secret of Tevunah,
Yaakov in the secret of Daas";
from Kesser Elyon, as is known.
And this is what it says:
"And Hashem of Hosts is exalted through judgment" —
for Yaakov our forefather, peace be upon him,
is a chariot for this attribute;
